items.title: Stanley Kay interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001
items.q: Guys like Ken Peplowski and Harry Allen and Bill Charlap, hey.

ctx.x: Yeah. Well Basie used to do that too with his charts, didn’t he? He would like tinker with them to make them sound like Basie.

Yeah. Well you know Neal brought in, Hefti, you know the story, “L’il Darlin.’” He went [scats]. And Basie said wait a minute, no, no, let’s do it that way. And it worked you see. So you’re always experimenting. You’re always trying to play new and fresh and do things — we try to write things for our soloists that they will like to play. Because you’ve got to believe in what you’re doing. I don’t do it up there, they do it up there. But I will comment. If I hear something I’ll discuss it. I’ll tell Sherrie, you…
Yeah. I didn’t get to ask you about being a club owner. Was that something that—
